positions.as_written: Take the history: pain on loading the affected compartment, an effusion appearing after activity, and whether anything catches or locks.
Assess the effusion, since a recurrent activity related effusion is one of the more reliable signs.
Assess the painful arc, since a lesion is loaded at a particular flexion angle and hurts there.
Assess the alignment, because it determines which compartment carries the load and therefore how a lesion behaves.
